name: Runner Extras - Integer Virtual Table Window
brief: Issues #2350, #3376 and #3438: the Integer system virtual table (2000000026) is computed on demand on the service tier, where IntegerDataProvider clamps every request to [-1000000000..1000000000]. The runner materialises rows per request too, so a closed span outside the base window is answered in full. This suite pins the runner-specific remainder: a span past the row cap is refused by name on every request path, and an open bound is answered from the base window rather than from BC's +-1e9.
description: What the Integer table itself answers - that Number 0, negatives, 250000 and -250000 are real rows, that a range filter yields every value in order, that an inverted range matches nothing - is plain BC behaviour and is covered upstream in the al-language corpus (Test Integer Virtual Table, codeunit 60368). This suite deliberately asserts none of that. It asserts only what exists because this is the runner: that AL_RUNNER_INTEGER_WINDOW_MAX_ROWS (500,000 by default) is a loud refusal rather than a short answer, and that a half-open filter whose closed end lies outside the base window -1000..100000 is refused rather than answered with zero rows.
